t: Minimum Operations to Make All Grid Elements Equal — 2D Difference Decomposition
o: Each operation adds 1 to a k×k block; make all cells equal or report -1. Example 1: two ops on the left 2×2 block equalize to 5. Example 2 (k=1): raise everything to the max, costing 4. Setting A = T - grid (target minus current), we ask when A is a sum of k×k all-ones blocks. Taking the 2D difference turns each block into four ±1 corner stamps, which makes the block multiplicities uniquely computable by a recurrence — feasibility and the minimal operation count then follow algebraically in O(mn).
k: With A = T - grid, A must equal a non-negative combination of k×k blocks; the 2D difference of A determines the block multiplicities uniquely.
The recurrence x[i][j] = D[i][j] + x[i][j-k] + x[i-k][j] - x[i-k][j-k] recovers multiplicities; they must be ≥ 0 at valid corners and 0 elsewhere.
T only enters through cell (0,0) and propagates to lattice points (i%k==0 and j%k==0), giving lower-bound/equality constraints on T; minimize ops by choosing the smallest feasible T.

a.i: Compute D = 2D difference of (-grid), recover base multiplicities by the stamp recurrence, derive constraints on T from lattice vs non-lattice and valid vs invalid corner cells, then sum multiplicities at the minimal feasible T.
s: Build base[][] via the recurrence with D from grid (no T yet).
Scan cells: valid lattice corners give T ≥ -base; invalid lattice corners force T = -base (conflict → -1); valid non-lattice cells need base ≥ 0; invalid non-lattice cells need base = 0.
Set T = max(maxGrid, lower bounds) or the forced equality (must dominate the lower bounds).
Answer = sum over valid lattice corners of base[i][j] + T.
a.t: O(mn) — two linear passes over the grid

w: This is a hard constructive/algebraic problem: derive the block-stamp decomposition on paper before coding. Pitfalls: mixing up the signs of the 2D difference, forgetting that T must also be ≥ max(grid) (so the final matrix is non-negative), and mishandling equality constraints at invalid lattice corners (conflicting equalities mean -1). Sanity checks: k=1 must always yield sum(max - g); a constant grid yields 0. Follow-up: allow decrement operations as well.
